In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions. (1) A novel joint routing and scheduling algorithm for TT traffic that takes into account AVB traffic and (2) an evaluation of the algorithm on synthetic and realistic test scenarios.
the joint routing and scheduling of TT and AVB traffic in a TSN network, such that both traffic classes are schedulable and that the worst case delay of AVB traffic is minimized.

the following questions: How can the routing and scheduling problem of TT traffic be solved in a joint manner such that AVB traffic is not affected by it? How does the routing of TT traffic affect the schedulability of AVB traffic?

our approach is the first that considers AVB traffic in the joint routing and scheduling problem of TSN.
our approach outperforms previous approaches by a significant margin, in terms of both schedulability and end to end delays.
our joint routing and scheduling algorithm can significantly improve the schedulability of AVB traffic.

we have proposed an approach that jointly routes and schedules TT traffic, such that the TT and AVB traffic are jointly schedulable.
we have developed a novel approach to jointly route and schedule TT traffic in a TSN network such that both TT traffic and AVB traffic are scheduled.

the joint routing and scheduling of TT and AVB traffic is possible, and that the resulting TT configurations can significantly reduce the worst case end to end delay of AVB traffic.
